items.anchor: On a compact sublevel, objective convergence implies distance to the solution set tends to zero.

items.anchor: generic or positive-measure failure
items.note: Stated as a Prop without proof: some finite convex objective with attained minimum and some pair 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1 have a large set S of failing starts (failingStarts: the starts x_0 from which the specified unit-first search, NonStrictLineSearch.fromMetric, with H_0 = I produces an admissible run whose values do not tend to the minimum value), in one of the two senses of the gap. Generic, read topologically: S is comeagre in some nonempty open set U of starting points (U \ S meagre). This is the weakest of the usual readings: it follows from failure on a comeagre set of all starts and from failure at every point of a nonempty open set, and for sets with the Baire property it is the same as being nonmeagre, the topological counterpart of positive measure. Positive-measure: S has positive Lebesgue (outer) measure. The failing starts of the constructions are countable, hence null and meagre (Ch12D.starts_null).
